subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: Should Signal edits remain distinct inbound turns carrying edit metadata, or supersede the original turn and suppress a second reply unless the edit explicitly mentions the agent?
rationale: signal-cli defines the transport relationship, but current OpenClaw contracts do not define how an edit mutates session history or triggers agent work, and the alternatives have materially different context and delivery semantics.

options.title: Distinct marked edit
options.body: Keep a unique edit event id, expose the original target id as structured metadata, and add an edited marker without rewriting prior history.

options.title: Supersede original turn
options.body: Introduce a session-level edit operation that invalidates or replaces the original turn and avoids duplicate processing.

options.title: Mention-gated group edits
options.body: Ingest non-mentioned group edits as context-only updates and dispatch only edits that explicitly mention the agent.

recommendation.title: Distinct marked edit
recommendation.body: Keep a unique edit event id, expose the original target id as structured metadata, and add an edited marker without rewriting prior history.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans Signal inbound dispatch and shared channel/session lifecycle seams where this person has the broadest recent history.
